findings.title: Google Meet fallback dereferences a possibly undefined destination calendar
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the array is empty, but line 119 reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. So when the location is Google Meet and no destination calendar is set (null or []), `create()` throws a TypeError and the booking fails instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Video references are saved without credentialId
findings.body: The `credentialId` mapping in `create()` was changed to `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Previously non-calendar (video) results kept `result.credentialId`. Now every video reference is stored with a null credentialId. handleCancelBooking.ts only deletes the video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set (around line 491), so cancelled bookings leave the Zoom/Daily/etc. meeting behind. The seated-cancellation video update path has the same dependency. Restore `result.credentialId` for the non-calendar branch.

findings.title: Destinations without credentialId lose their externalId and can create duplicate events
findings.body: For destinations without a credentialId, `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the destination's externalId. The result therefore has `externalId` undefined, and the booking reference is stored with a null externalCalendarId. Google picks its calendar only by credentialId, so the event goes to 'primary' and later update/delete cannot find the right calendar. The previous code stored `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. In addition, this loop runs once per destination against the same list of credentials of that type, so N such destinations and K credentials produce N×K events.

findings.title: Per-destination calendar is only honored by the Google service; other calendar apps still use the organizer's calendar
findings.body: CalendarManager calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. The destination externalId is only attached to the returned result, so the calendar implementation never sees which calendar this credential should write to. Only the Google service resolves its calendar by credentialId. Lark (googlecalendar-style `destinationCalendar[0]` at larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts line 129), Office365 (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts line 75) and CalDAV (lib/CalendarService.ts line 161) always use the first destination, which for a collective event is usually the organizer's calendar. A team member's Lark or O365 credential therefore targets the organizer's calendar ID with the member's token, which fails. The collective-event fix works only for Google.

findings.title: CalDAV reports success when no event was written for a team member
findings.body: The filter keeps only calendars whose externalId equals the first destination's externalId. For a team member's CalDAV account that URL does not exist, so the filtered list is empty. `responses` is then empty, `responses.some((r) => !r.ok)` is false, and the function returns a uid as if the event was created. CalendarManager records success=true, the member never gets the event, and no error is logged.

findings.title: updateEvent calendar fallback is always undefined
findings.body: The fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. This branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate compares against null/undefined and never matches. The result is `calendarId: undefined` for `events.update`. Booking references with a null externalCalendarId (legacy rows and rows written by the no-credentialId branch in EventManager) can no longer be updated, which breaks reschedule and location edits. The previous code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`.

findings.title: deleteEvent fallback never finds the destination calendar and defaults to primary
findings.body: Same dead predicate as in updateEvent: `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it always returns undefined. `calendarId` then becomes 'primary' (line 322), so cancelling a booking whose reference has no externalCalendarId deletes from the user's primary calendar, not the calendar the event was created on, and the event remains on the destination calendar.

findings.title: Hangout patch still uses selectedCalendar, which can now be undefined
findings.body: The insert now falls back with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `events.patch` (line 168) still passes the raw `selectedCalendar`. That value is undefined when no destination matches the credentialId, so the patch is sent without a calendarId. The patch is fire-and-forget with no callback or catch, so the failure is unhandled and the hangout link description is silently not updated. Use the same fallback in the patch.

findings.title: Team members' calendars are dropped when the organizer and event type have no destination calendar
findings.body: `destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one (around line 1067). `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so every collective member's calendar is discarded. This is the scenario the PR is meant to fix. The array may also start with a team member's calendar, which the calendar services then treat as the organizer's main calendar.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference of each instance
findings.body: The PR changed the top-level logic to iterate over all calendar references, but this recurring-cancel path still uses `updBooking.references.find(...)`, so only the first calendar reference per instance is considered. For a collective recurring booking with a second calendar reference (for example the team member's), that event is never deleted. The calls go to every calendar credential with the first reference's uid, which fails silently for the other accounts.

findings.title: Recurring deletions are repeated once per calendar reference
findings.body: This block sits inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. Each iteration re-runs the same deletion of every updated booking across all calendar credentials. With two calendar references and a recurring series, each instance's event is deleted twice (or more), producing duplicate API calls and duplicate entries in `apiDeletes`. The deletion should run once, outside the loop.

findings.title: Inverted condition: organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled
findings.body: The original `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` spreads `slug` when billing is disabled. The rewrite `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` spreads it only when billing is enabled. The behavior is inverted for both self-hosted and cloud deployments, and the change is unrelated to the destination-calendar work in this PR. Revert to the original predicate.

findings.title: loadUsers error handling turns client errors into 500s and leaks Prisma messages
findings.body: The new try/catch wraps the whole user-loading path. The `dynamicUserList` validation at line 728 throws a plain Error, which is not an HttpError, so it is rethrown as HttpError 500 'Unable to load users', losing the message and the 4xx status. Conversely, Prisma known-request errors are rethrown as HttpError 400 with the raw Prisma message, which exposes internal details. The old code let these errors propagate unchanged.

findings.title: Webhook payload destinationCalendar changes from object to array without a breaking-change note
findings.body: The event object is sent as-is in BOOKING_CREATED/REQUESTED webhook payloads (`...evt` in sendPayload). `destinationCalendar` changes from a DestinationCalendar object (or null) to an array (or null here, [] in other paths). Existing webhook consumers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` will break. The e2e test was edited to expect `[]` for BOOKING_REJECTED while still expecting `null` for BOOKING_CREATED, so the payload is now inconsistent across events and the contract change is undocumented.

findings.title: Organization relation dropped from dynamic-group user query without explanation
findings.body: The `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` selection was removed from the dynamic-user query. The PR does not explain why or add a replacement. If any downstream code in this handler reads `users[i].organization` for dynamic group bookings, it now receives undefined. The removal should be justified or reverted.

findings.title: Error logging removed from updateAllCalendarEvents catch block
findings.body: The `console.error(message)` call was removed. The catch now returns fallback results with success=false and emits no log, so calendar update failures disappear silently. The `message` string is still built but never output.

findings.title: No tests cover the new multi-destination create/update/cancel logic
findings.body: The PR states no tests were added. The new multi-destination logic in createAllCalendarEvents and updateAllCalendarEvents, and the Google calendar-id selection, are where most of the defects above sit (null-calendar regressions, dead predicates, lost credentialIds). A unit test per destination shape (with and without credentialId, empty and multiple destinations) would catch these.
